chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Atiyyah ibn Rustam, who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who performs zihar with his wife. He said, 'If it is in the context of an oath, there is no penalty upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zihar if it is considered an oath?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the juristic nuance of zihar is clarified by linking it directly to the nature of the oath (yamin); if the utterance is classified strictly as an oath, the specific expiation for zihar is not immediately due. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle that zihar is essentially an oath of abstinence, and its legal consequences depend on whether the speaker intended it as a distinct declaration or merely as an oath. The hadith thus provides a precise condition for when the kaffarah of zihar applies, distinguishing it from general oath expiation.
